Let \(a=BC\). From the Law of Sines,
\[
\frac{a}{\sin 2\theta}=\frac{9}{\sin\theta}\implies a=18\cos\theta.
\]
Also,
\[
c=AB=\frac{9\sin 3\theta}{\sin\theta}=27-36\sin^2\theta.
\]
Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) and \(\cos\theta=a/18\),
\[
c=27-36\left(1-\frac{a^2}{324}\right)=\frac{a^2}{9}-9.
\]
Since \(c\) is an integer, \(a^2\) must be divisible by \(9\), so \(3\mid a\).

Also \(\angle C=180^\circ-3\theta>0\), so \(\theta<60^\circ\). Thus \(\cos\theta>1/2\), giving
\[
9<a<18.
\]
The integer multiples of \(3\) in this range are \(12,15\). The smallest is \(a=12\), which gives \(c=7\), a valid integer side length.

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
